title: Doppelkopf in 5 minutes
sub: The card game from every pub in Germany. Two against two – except nobody knows at first who is with whom.
goal: The goal: Win more than half of the card points with your team, so at least 121 of 240. Who your partner is, only the cards will tell.
setupLead: You need exactly 4 players and a Doppelkopf deck of 48 cards.
deckAlt: Each suit – clubs, spades, hearts and diamonds – has 9, 10, jack, queen, king and ace, and every card twice.
deckP: Each of the four suits ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦ has 9, 10, jack, queen, king and ace – and every card comes twice. That’s where the name comes from (“double head”). You can buy a Doppelkopf deck, or take two standard decks and keep only the 9s and up.
rankP: J = jack, Q = queen, K = king, A = ace.
dealP: Everyone gets 12 cards, best 3 at a time. The player to the dealer’s left leads the first card. The next round is dealt by the next player clockwise.
teamLead: Doppelkopf is two against two. But the cards decide who is together – not where you sit.
teamAlt: The two players with a queen of clubs are Re, the other two are Kontra.
teamP1: Re are the two players holding a queen of clubs (♣Q). The other two are Kontra.
teamP2: At first you only know which team you are on yourself. The rest comes out during play: at the latest when a queen of clubs hits the table or someone calls “Re” or “Kontra”.
teamP3: If one player has both queens of clubs, it’s a wedding.
trumpLead: This is the most important part of the game. More than half of the cards are trumps, and a trump beats everything else.
trumpAlt: Trumps from high to low: ten of hearts, queen of clubs, queen of spades, queen of hearts, queen of diamonds, jack of clubs, jack of spades, jack of hearts, jack of diamonds, ace of diamonds, ten of diamonds, king of diamonds, nine of diamonds.
tr1p: The “Dulle”. It is the highest trump.
tr2p: In the order ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦. The queen of clubs is also called “the old one”.
tr4p: Ace, 10, king, 9. The ace of diamonds is called the “fox”.
trumpWarn: Careful: Queens, jacks and the ten of hearts no longer belong to their suit. The queen of spades is a trump, not a spade.
plainP: Cards that aren’t trumps belong to the three plain suits. In each one it goes: ace, then 10, then king, then 9.
plainAlt: Plain suits from high to low: clubs ace, 10, king, 9. Spades ace, 10, king, 9. Hearts ace, king, 9.
plain6: only 6 cards, the 10 is a trump
trickLead: Whoever’s turn it is leads a card. Then everyone adds one card, clockwise. The four cards make a trick.
dqs: Following suit means playing the same as the first card. Trump on trump, spade on spade.
by1: Then you must follow suit. Which matching card you play is up to you.
bn1: Then you may play any card: a trump to win the trick, or another card you want to get rid of.
dnext: Whoever wins the trick takes the four cards and leads the next one.
win1: If there is a trump in the trick, the highest trump wins.
win2: Otherwise the highest card of the suit that was led wins. Other suits don’t count.
win3: If the same card is in the trick twice, the one played first wins.
trickAlt: A trick: the ace of spades is led, followed by the ten of spades, the jack of diamonds and the king of spades. The jack of diamonds is a trump and wins.
trickP: The jack of diamonds wins: whoever played it had no spades left and was allowed to trump. They take all four cards, here 27 points.
countLead: After 12 tricks, each team counts the cards in its tricks. Each card is worth this many points:
valuesAlt: Ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2, nine 0 points.
countP: That makes 240 points in total. Re wins with 121 points. Kontra only needs 120, so a tie goes to Kontra.
qLead: Quick test in a normal game. One card has been led, you add yours.
callLead: Think your team will win? Then say so. It earns more points – but whatever you call, you have to make.
reP: By calling “Re” or “Kontra” you say: my team will win. It also gives away which team you are on. You may call as long as you still have at least 11 cards, so until you play your second card.
absP: After that your team can make further calls. Each step is allowed one card later than the one before:
a2m: The others get fewer than 90 points.
a3m: The others get fewer than 60 points.
a4m: The others get fewer than 30 points.
a5m: The others don’t win a single trick.
absNote: Calling “no 90” also counts as calling Re or Kontra. A team that doesn’t make its call has lost. And: if only Kontra makes a call, Re already wins with 120 points.
scoreLead: After each game there are game points. The winning team adds up:
s3: per level the losers didn’t reach: under 90, under 60, under 30, black.
s4: per call of Re or Kontra, no matter who made it.
s5: per further call no 90, no 60, no 30, black, no matter who made it.
extraLead: These only exist in a normal game. Each team gets them, even the losing team. The losers’ extra points are subtracted from the total.
x1p: You win an ace of diamonds from the other team in your trick.
x2p: The jack of clubs wins the last trick.
x3p: A trick worth at least 40 points.
payP: Both winners add the total to their score, both losers subtract it. Play a fixed number of rounds, for example 24. Whoever is ahead then wins.
exH: Example: Re called and wins 185 to 55 points.
ex2: Kontra only has 55 points: under 90 and under 60.
exSum: The Re players get 4 points each, the Kontra players lose 4 each.
specLead: Before the first trick, everyone in turn, starting to the dealer’s left, says “healthy” or “reservation”. With a reservation you announce a special game. A solo beats a wedding.
weddingP: You have both queens of clubs. Announce it. Whoever wins a trick first becomes your partner – this has to happen within the first three tricks. If you win all three yourself, you play alone against the others. If you keep the wedding to yourself, you play a “silent solo”.
soloP: One player plays alone against three and decides what is trump:
so1p: Only the queens are trumps, in the order ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦. In the suits it goes ace, 10, king, jack, 9.
so2p: Only the jacks are trumps. In the suits it goes ace, 10, king, queen, 9.
so3p: Like a normal game, but the chosen suit takes the place of diamonds. In a clubs solo, the clubs are trumps and diamonds are a plain suit.
so4p: No trumps at all. In every suit it goes ace, 10, king, queen, jack, 9.
soloScore: Scoring works as usual, just without extra points. The soloist is Re. They win or lose the total three times, each opponent once.
varLead: Almost every group plays a little differently. Agree beforehand on what applies to you. These rules are especially common:
v1p: Leave out the 9s and play with 40 cards. Everyone gets 10. You can switch to these rules at the top of the page.
v2h: The second Dulle beats the first
v2p: If both tens of hearts are in a trick, the second one wins instead of the first.
v3p: Whoever has both aces of diamonds may make them the highest trumps, even above the Dulle.
v4p: Whoever has 3 trumps or fewer may hand them over. Whoever takes them voluntarily becomes their partner and gives back the same number of cards.
v5p: Whoever has 5 or more nines may ask for a redeal.
v6p: Under tournament rules everyone has to play one solo within a series of rounds.
stLead: Once you know the rules, these customs help you win more often. The bots on the game page follow them too – so you can recognise them while you play.
t1p: There are 26 trumps. With 7 or more, your hand is strong. Keep track of which high ones have been played, especially the Dullen and the queens of clubs.
t2p: Each plain suit has only 8 cards, hearts only 6. The first time round everyone usually follows suit, after that it often gets trumped. So play your ace the first time, black aces before the ace of hearts. A second round of hearts hardly ever goes through.
t3p: Your partner doesn’t know you are their partner. So: Re leads trumps (so the other queen of clubs can win), Kontra leads plain suits. As Re, play the queen of clubs as soon as it wins a trick. And an early call gives your team away at once.
t4p: If your partner is sure to win a trick, add an ace or a 10. That way lots of points end up with your team.
t5p: Don’t play your ace of diamonds while the other team can still beat it. Otherwise they get an extra point.
t6p: Roughly count the points. If you know your team already has 100, you play the last tricks differently.
t7p: A call is worth 2 extra points – for the other team too if you lose. With lots of high trumps it pays off.
t8p: If you can’t follow a plain suit and want to trump, use at least a jack while opponents still play after you. With the fox or the ten of diamonds you easily get overtrumped.
c1d: Win at least 121 of 240 points with your team.
c2d: Re = the two with a queen of clubs. Kontra = the rest.
c3d: Ten of hearts, all queens, all jacks, diamonds (each ♣ ♠ ♥ ♦).
c5d: You must. If you can’t: any card.
c6d: Highest trump, else highest card of the suit led. Same cards: the first.
c8d: Re/Kontra while you have 11 cards, then no 90, 60, 30, black.
shLead: Let the others at the table scan the code. Everyone can then pick their own language.
foot: Good cards! And remember: the Dulle wins – almost always.

quiz.sameCard: The same card twice: the one played first wins.
quiz.bothTrumpHigher: Both are trumps, and {mine} is higher than {led}.
quiz.bothTrumpLower: Both are trumps, but {led} is higher than {mine}.
quiz.trumpBeats: {mine} is a trump, {led} is not. A trump beats any plain card.
quiz.trumpLed: {led} is a trump. Only a higher trump beats it, and {mine} is not a trump.
quiz.suitHigher: Same suit, and {mine} is higher than {led}.
quiz.suitLower: Same suit, but {led} is higher than {mine}.
quiz.otherSuit: {mine} is neither a trump nor the same suit as {led}. It can’t win.

game.title: Play Doppelkopf against bots
game.sub: Doppelkopf against three computer players, right in your browser. Works offline too.
game.levelHelp: Normal plays by the conventions from the rules page: Re leads trumps, Kontra plain suits, the queen of clubs shows up early – so you can tell who is with whom. Strong plays the same way, but before every card it works through how the hidden cards could be distributed.

soloHelp.clubs: Like a normal game, but clubs instead of diamonds.
soloHelp.spades: Like a normal game, but spades instead of diamonds.
soloHelp.hearts: Like a normal game, but hearts instead of diamonds.
soloHelp.diamonds: Trumps as in a normal game – but you play alone.

game.reserveP: Healthy means a normal game. Or play alone against the three others: open the solos.
game.reserveWedding: You have both queens of clubs! Announce a wedding to find a partner – or say healthy and play a silent solo against the other three.
game.normalGame: Normal game: Re are the two with a queen of clubs.
game.youSilent: Silent solo: you play alone against the other three. They don’t know yet.
game.weddingOn: {name} has a wedding: whoever wins a trick first plays with {name}.
game.youWedding: Your wedding: whoever wins a trick first plays with you.
game.alone: {name} finds no partner and plays alone.
game.youAlone: No partner: you play alone against the three others.
game.reveal: {name} plays a queen of clubs: Re.
game.yourLead: Your lead: tap a card, then tap it again or press “Play”.
game.cantFollow: You can’t follow suit: play any card.
game.mustFollow: {card} isn’t allowed – you have to follow {what}.
game.noWinner: Both parties missed their calls. No game points.
game.soloTriple: The soloist gets or loses it three times.
game.ctaP: Play right here against three bots – they play exactly by these rules.
